title: Verifier‑Assisted versus LLM‑Only Pre‑deployment Network‑Change Validation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We measured whether integrating a deterministic pre‑deployment verifier (with at most one automated repair) increases the fraction of intent‑driven configuration proposals that pass semantic validation compared with accepting a single LLM candidate. In a preregistered paired design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) we executed 300 paired intents (100 per difficulty stratum) using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic NetOps validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Each pair evaluated one shared_initial candidate under two conditions: baseline (accept single shot) and guarded (deterministic validation and ≤1 automated repair). Results: baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.9966667), guarded 300/300 (1.0); paired contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00,0.01] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000). Under the supplied synthetic suite and model, single‑shot generation was near ceiling, limiting observable marginal rescue by the guarded pipeline. All preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts are archived with the study id.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for NetOps tasks such as translating operator intent into device configurations, synthesizing templates, and automating routine repairs. For operational deployment, semantic guarantees (correct sequencing of operations, preservation of reachability/policy invariants, and avoidance of forbidden edits) are required in addition to syntactic well‑formedness. To reduce operational risk, hybrid generate→validate→repair architectures pair LLMs with deterministic validators and bounded automated repair. The practical benefit of such hybrid architectures depends on the chosen estimand (what is held fixed), the generator's single‑shot quality, the validator's coverage, and the allowed repair budget.

We preregistered a paired experiment (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) to quantify the deterministic rescue utility of adding a verifier plus at most one automated repair when the same single LLM candidate is evaluated under two treatments. For each intent the pipeline produced one shared_initial candidate with gpt-5-mini and compared: (a) baseline — accept that single candidate, and (b) guarded — run deterministic validation and allow at most one automated repair that is revalidated. The central research question: does a deterministic verifier plus ≤1 automated repair increase the probability that a single LLM candidate passes semantic pre‑deployment validation compared with accepting that same single candidate without repair?

Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered paired evaluation isolating deterministic rescue utility under a shared_initial estimand; (2) a complete execution and analysis bundle including validator traces and the single automated repair transcript archived with the run; and (3) an artifact‑grounded interpretation of estimand conditioning, observed ceiling effects, and operational implications for NetOps pipelines.
sections.related_work:
Surveys and systems work document extensive activity at the intersection of LLMs and NetOps, covering intent‑based translation, configuration synthesis, repair, and tool‑augmented agentic frameworks [W4416927413; W4411015066; W4404240614; W4402742293]. Prior systems papers show that validator assistance and constrained repair can improve correctness, but reported gains depend strongly on task distributions, validator expressiveness, and whether comparisons permit additional independent model draws. Tool‑augmented architectures (planner‑centric, ReAct, and other orchestration strategies) enable calls to external validators and multi‑step workflows, but head‑to‑head, large‑scale evaluations that disentangle generator sampling effects from deterministic validator rescue are scarce [doi:10.1609/aaai.v40i40.40676; W4389518608].

Practitioner studies reveal operator skepticism about direct deployability despite high syntactic correctness in controlled evaluations, emphasizing the need for semantic checks that encode sequencing, protected resources, and reachability invariants [W7167855398; W4416927413]. Our study targets the methodological gap created when prior comparisons conflate validator rescue with benefits from resampling: by conditioning on a single shared_initial candidate per paired intent we measure only deterministic validator/repair rescue, an estimator aligned to operational policies that constrain model calls.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration, estimand, and confirmatory design. The study preregistration (cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) fixed the primary estimand as the absolute paired difference in the unflagged verifier‑pass proportion (guarded minus baseline) computed on paired cases that evaluate the same shared_initial candidate. The confirmatory design required 300 analyzable pairs (100 per difficulty stratum: low/medium/high), explicit inclusion/exclusion rules, and a deterministic paired analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1). The preregistration specified an optional pilot (n = 60) for discordance estimation; that pilot was not executed and no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed — this deviation is explicitly noted and archived.

Task generation and synthetic benchmark. Tasks were generated deterministically by the registered task generator into a synthetic_topology_suite and stratified by metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count). Each task manifest includes an initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, and intent constraints (examples: 'shutdown_configure_restore' and 'paired_link_atomic_mtu_change'). The synthetic suite enforces invariants (protected_interfaces, preserve_unspecified_state) that the validator checks; representative tasks and shared_initial responses for multiple difficulty patterns are included in the archived run bundle to illustrate typical validator diagnostics.

Shared_initial protocol, model, and orchestration. To isolate deterministic rescue we used a shared_initial protocol: a single generation per pair (gpt-5-mini) was produced and reused for both baseline and guarded conditions. The guarded pipeline applied deterministic_netops_validator_v5 to the shared_initial candidate; if flagged the pipeline invoked at most one automated repair attempt (repair budget ≤1), producing an edited candidate that was revalidated deterministically. The baseline pipeline accepted the same shared_initial candidate unmodified. This design prevents any benefit from drawing independent alternative generator candidates and therefore quantifies only deterministic validation/repair rescue under single‑call operational constraints.

Validator, scoring rule, and repair policy. deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implements preregistered full_intent_constraint_validation: deterministic checks for sequencing constraints (must_be_down_for_fields), required_command_count, preservation of unspecified state, encoded reachability invariants for the synthetic topology, and forbidden‑template protections (protected_interfaces). Scoring for the primary estimand is binary (unflagged == pass). The automated repair is a constrained, localized edit operator that attempts to insert or reorder required sequencing commands; repair attempts and validator decisions were logged and archived. Repair was limited to ≤1 invocation per pair by design to measure bounded rescue.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation. The hosted adapter completed the confirmatory run with completed_episode_count = 600 and complete_pair_count = 300; model_calls_used = 301 (300 shared_initial generations + 1 repair call). Stage auditing recorded 300 shared_initial_generation events and 1 repair event; no provider outages, failed episodes, or unscorable episodes were observed under the preregistered missingness rules. The contamination summary is empty and deterministic reconciliation confirms all episode and provider‑call accounting.

Marginal and paired outcomes. Condition summary (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes = 299/300 (0.9966666667), guarded successes = 300/300 (1.0). Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n11 = 299, n10 = 1 (guarded‑only), n01 = 0 (baseline‑only), n00 = 0. The pre‑registered confirmatory exact McNemar two‑sided test returned p = 1.0. Absolute paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0033333333333332993. A paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI computed with B = 10000 resamples and seed = 1729 yields [0.00, 0.01]. Per‑stratum breakdown: low = 100/100 baseline & guarded; medium = 100/100 baseline & guarded; high = baseline 99/100 vs guarded 100/100.

Repair diagnostic and transcript summary. The single discordant episode (n10 = 1) triggered the permitted automated repair. Validator traces attribute the initial flag to an omitted sequencing command required by the intent (a must_be_down_for_fields violation): the shared_initial candidate omitted an 'admin down' step before changing VLAN/MTU. The repair routine inserted the missing sequencing command; deterministic revalidation then reported valid == true. The concise semantic description of this repair is reported here; the archived run bundle contains the full low‑level repair provider trace and the validator trace for forensic inspection.

Statistical interpretation and sensitivity. The near‑ceiling baseline single‑shot success rate produced only one discordant pair, constraining inferential sensitivity: the exact test p‑value of 1.0 reflects the paucity of discordant evidence under the shared_initial estimand. The bootstrap CI bounds the plausible absolute paired improvement at ≤1 percentage point in this experimental context. These findings do not imply equivalence under alternative estimands that permit resampling or iterative generation, which can exploit generator variance and therefore materially increase rescue opportunities compared with the single‑call shared_initial protocol.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation of the shared_initial estimand. Conditioning on a single LLM draw corresponds to operational policies that limit model calls per change (cost, latency, or process constraints). Under that policy the guarded pipeline measures only deterministic validator and bounded repair rescue applied to the same candidate. Permitting independent resampling or verifier‑directed candidate selection changes the estimand: such workflows exploit generator variance and often yield larger gains than deterministic repair alone. We therefore emphasize that our reported null discordance under shared_initial does not generalize to resampling‑permitting policies.

Ceiling effects, pilot omission, and power consequences. The preregistered power target assumed baseline discordance sufficient to detect a 10 percentage‑point absolute improvement with 80% power. Because the optional pilot (n = 60) for discordance estimation was not executed, the main run encountered a near‑ceiling baseline (299/300) and consequently minimal discordance (m = 1). This reduced sensitivity to detect the originally targeted effect size. We recommend that future confirmatory designs execute a small pilot under the same task generator and sampling frame before fixing the main N, or alternatively adopt an estimand that increases discordance sensitivity (e.g., allow resampling or enlarge repair budget).

Validator coverage and failure‑mode dependence. The observed dominant failure mode was a sequencing omission; other classes (reachability violations, protected‑ACL removal, or forbidden‑template edits) were not observed at scale on this synthetic suite. The marginal value of a guarded pipeline therefore depends on the failure‑mode distribution in real deployments and on the validator's encoded invariants. A richer validator or a task distribution with more reachability or template‑violation failures would likely increase observed rescue rates.

Practical recommendations for NetOps pipelines. If operations constrain single model calls, deterministic validation plus a bounded automated repair can correct localized omissions (as observed here). If policy permits additional model calls, evaluate resampling or verifier‑guided candidate selection under a different estimand because these strategies can yield larger improvements. For higher assurance, consider expanding repair budgets, permitting iterative repair cycles, employing stronger domain‑adapted generators, or increasing validator coverage of semantic invariants.

Reproducibility and artifact grounding. All preregistration documents, task manifests, model configuration, raw responses, provider traces, validator traces, and analysis CSVs (condition_summary.csv and paired_contingency_table.csv) are archived with the study id. Analysis parameters (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729) and exact executor outputs are recorded; deterministic reconciliation confirms episode accounting and provider call audits. The archived run bundle contains the low‑level repair provider trace for the single repaired episode; the manuscript reports a concise semantic summary of that repair while the full trace is available in the artifact bundle for independent recomputation and forensic inspection.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired comparison between a verifier‑assisted pipeline (deterministic validator + ≤1 automated repair) and accepting a single‑shot LLM candidate under the shared_initial estimand on 300 synthetic NetOps intents using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Baseline single‑shot generation produced 299/300 unflagged verifier passes and the guarded pipeline 300/300, yielding an absolute paired improvement of 0.00333 (exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.01]). The single repaired episode corrected a sequencing omission. The near‑ceiling baseline limits inferential sensitivity to small absolute improvements under the shared_initial estimand. We release the preregistration, execution and analysis artifacts, representative task manifests, and validator traces in the archived run bundle to enable reproducible follow‑ups that vary estimand choice, model strength, topology realism, or repair strategies.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were generated by the preregistered deterministic task generator; real‑world heterogeneity may expose different failure modes and increase verifier marginal utility.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs or richer/diverse validators.

Ceiling effect: baseline single‑shot performance was near 100% on this suite (299/300), producing limited discordance and reduced power to detect small absolute improvements relative to larger pre‑specified targets.
Pilot not executed: the preregistered pilot intended for discordance estimation and power calibration was not run; no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed.

Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions the estimand on a single LLM candidate and therefore does not measure verifier benefit that would arise from allowing independent alternative LLM candidates per condition (resampling or iterative generation).
Repair budget: the guarded condition permitted at most one automated repair per pair; larger or iterative repair strategies may yield different outcomes.
